_comment: The watch list for scripts/ced-watch.js. Every entry is a FIRST-PARTY College
Board URL. Secondary coverage (blogs, vendor summaries, teacher forums) is
deliberately excluded: it restates AP Central late and paraphrases it wrong,
so it generates churn without adding a single fact you could act on.
Every URL here was confirmed to resolve before it was added. Do not add a URL
you have not opened. A permanently 404ing source reports UNREACHABLE every
week, and a weekly alarm that is always wrong is how a watcher gets ignored.
kind:  'html' stores normalized visible text, so the PR diff is readable.
'pdf'  stores sha256 + length only, because parsing PDFs would mean a
dependency and the only question worth asking of these files is
critical: surfaces at the top of the report. Reserve it for documents whose
revision would invalidate published course content.

sources.label: AP Networking Course Framework (PDF)
sources.why: The single highest-value signal in this file. AP Networking is still in pilot until the 2027-28 national launch, so this framework can still be revised. A revision here is the one event that can invalidate the 22 published topic pages.

sources.label: About AP Networking
sources.why: Unit titles, skill categories, and launch timing. First page to change when the framework moves.

sources.label: Adopt AP Networking
sources.why: Adoption requirements and equipment expectations. Changes here are buying-decision changes for a teacher.

sources.label: AP Networking Credential
sources.why: Industry certification alignment (CompTIA Network+, Cisco CCNA and CCST). The stable, fully public part of the spec.

sources.label: AP Career Kickstart pilots
sources.why: Carries pilot ELIGIBILITY, which is the current ceiling on the AP Networking market. The 2026-27 pilot is restricted to prior AP Networking and AP Cybersecurity pilot schools. Any widening of that rule is a direct revenue event.

sources.label: AP Career Kickstart hub
sources.why: Where a fourth Career Kickstart course would be announced first.

sources.label: AP Cybersecurity Course and Exam Description (PDF)
sources.why: AP Cybersecurity reached national launch in 2026-27, so this is a live CED against a course already sold.

sources.label: AP Cybersecurity course page
sources.why: Five units and the three spiralled skills (Analyze Risk, Mitigate Risk, Detect Attacks).

sources.label: AP Cybersecurity Exam
sources.why: Exam format and weighting for a first-national-launch course, which is exactly where College Board still adjusts.

sources.label: AP Cybersecurity classroom resources
sources.why: What College Board gives teachers for free. It sets the floor the paid Teacher Bundle has to clear.

sources.label: AP CSA future revisions
sources.why: The page that announced the 10-unit to 4-unit rebuild. If CSA moves again, it says so here first.

sources.label: AP Computer Science A course page
sources.why: Course-level framing and links to the current CED.

sources.label: AP Computer Science Principles course page
sources.why: Five big ideas and the Create performance task framing.

sources.label: AP CSP Course and Exam Description (PDF)
sources.why: CSP is a mature course and this rarely moves, which is exactly why a change is worth hearing about.

sources.label: AP course and exam changes (program-wide)
sources.why: The program-wide announcement page. Catches a course revision that has not reached the per-course pages yet.

sources.label: AP exam dates
sources.why: Drives the promo calendar. Task 70 exists because a stale seasonal date sat live on the storefront.
